question.text: SEBI's corporate governance requirements for market intermediaries include:

answer.text: Board composition requirements, internal controls, compliance officer appointment, and periodic reporting to SEBI
No specific governance requirements for intermediaries
Governance requirements only for listed companies

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI's broader governance framework for registered intermediaries, market intermediaries are expected to meet a combination of corporate-governance requirements: prescribed board composition and qualifications, robust internal controls and risk management, appointment of a compliance officer, and periodic reporting/disclosures to SEBI and exchanges. These obligations support investor protection and orderly market functioning. The Trap: The requirements are not limited to financial reporting, and they are not restricted to listed companies only — registered intermediaries are subject to a governance package even when unlisted. It is also incorrect to say SEBI imposes no governance requirements on intermediaries. Note: The cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages discuss SEBI's general jurisdiction and broker compliance activities but do not present the combined corporate-governance package (board composition, compliance officer, internal controls, periodic reporting) for intermediaries. The framing above reflects general SEBI intermediary-governance principles rather than a workbook citation.
